readout.summary: Everyone expects Memphis to win; the split is whether it covers about 17.5. Memphis (8-3, 5-0 at home) leads the nation in total offense (520.8 yards per game) and scores 38.5 a game, while Temple is 2-9 and allows about 29 points. Covers, The Rx and Fox's model back Memphis -17.5/-18.5, saying the Tigers are motivated after a late collapse and Temple is playing out the string. Predictem and Doc's Sports take Temple +17.5: Memphis allows 209.7 rushing yards a game (131st) and Temple runs for 185.5. Memphis's defense has allowed 30+ in four of its last five, so a backdoor cover is the risk. Temple QB Ajani Sheppard is listed questionable (undisclosed); no Memphis injuries were reported.

picks.note: Memphis more motivated; Temple playing out a 2-9 season
Memphis offense gets back on track; Temple lacks firepower

readout.summary: The consensus is Texas, and most analysts expect a cover of about 11. Texas (9-2, five straight wins, top-5) is chasing an SEC title game spot behind a defense Covers says leads the country in net adjusted EPA per play; Arch Manning is off his best game. Texas A&M (4-7, 1-7 SEC, four straight losses) still hasn't settled on Marcel Reed (8 TD, 9 INT) or Brady Hart at quarterback and ranks 114th in passing offense. CBS, Predictem, Sports Betting Dime and Covers back Texas -10.5 to -11.5; models give Texas 79-82%. BettorsInsider dissents with A&M +11.5 and the Under 40.5, arguing Texas hasn't proven it can blow teams out on the road. A&M has several players ruled out, including WR Terry Bussey and two offensive linemen; Texas edges Colin Simmons and Richard Wesley are questionable.

picks.note: Aggies lack firepower to compete for four quarters
